spec.hypothesis: Stocks whose latest quarterly earnings beat the same quarter a year earlier by an unusually large amount (high SUE) outperform sector- and beta-matched peers over the next month; large misses underperform.
spec.rationale: Post-earnings-announcement drift: investors underreact to earnings news (Bernard and Thomas, 1989; widely replicated). The effect is reported to be weaker in large caps and in recent decades, so a small positive result is the realistic best case.
spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and shadow-test for 24 monthly rebalances. If any gate fails: close H1. Do not retry other horizons, freshness windows or thresholds on 2018-2026.

spec.hypothesis: Stocks whose insiders were net open-market buyers over the last 90 days outperform sector- and beta-matched peers over the next month; heavy net insider selling predicts underperformance.
spec.rationale: Insiders know their firms best; open-market purchases in particular carry information (Lakonishok and Lee, 2001; Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski, 2012). Sales are noisier because insiders sell for many non-informational reasons.
spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: record as qualified, but forward testing needs a daily Form 4 feed (not included yet). If any gate fails: close H2; do not retry other windows or thresholds on 2018-2026.

forward.reason: the SEC publishes these data sets quarterly, so a live signal would be months stale. Forward testing needs a daily Form 4 feed, which this kit does not include.

spec.hypothesis: The monthly low-volatility composite (calmer stocks beat sector- and beta-matched peers) continues forward.
spec.rationale: Historical test on 2018-2026 was close but failed (Sharpe 0.21 vs 0.25; effect beyond beta not significant). Its features are closed for historical testing, so the only honest remaining test is forward, as an exploratory strategy that can never be promoted.
spec.decision_rule: Exploratory only: watch for 24 monthly rebalances. If forward results clearly beat the historical ones, write a NEW pre-registered hypothesis to test on later data; never promote this one directly.

spec.hypothesis: A monthly, long-only cross-asset trend rule (hold each of 9 asset-class ETFs only while its 12-month return beats T-bills, otherwise hold T-bills) delivers a Sharpe ratio close to a 60/40 stock/bond portfolio with shallower drawdowns.
spec.rationale: Time-series momentum is documented across asset classes over more than a century (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen 2017). Its main value is cutting exposure in prolonged declines. The 2017-2026 test window is short, so this confirms a known effect rather than discovering one.

signal.description: 12-month total return of each ETF versus BIL

spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 24 months against 60/40. If any gate fails: close H3; do not try other lookbacks, asset lists or weightings on this data.

spec.hypothesis: Holding the S&P 500 members with the strongest 12-month gains (skipping the latest month), equal-weighted and rebalanced monthly, beats both SPY and an equal-weighted S&P 500 after costs.
spec.rationale: Medium-term momentum (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993) is among the most replicated return patterns. Skipping the latest month avoids short-term reversal. Comparing with the equal-weighted universe separates the momentum effect from simply equal-weighting smaller S&P members. Prior evidence on this data: 126-day momentum showed a weak positive raw IC (t about 1.6), so a strong result is not expected.

signal.description: return from 252 to 21 trading days ago

spec.prior_evidence: 126-day momentum had a weak positive raw IC; this 12-1 construction was not tested.
spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 24 months against SPY. If any gate fails: close H4; do not try other lookbacks, skip periods or portfolio sizes on this data.

spec.hypothesis: Buying S&P 500 stocks right after a big, fast breakout (5-day gain of at least 8%, a new 20-day closing high, volume at least 1.5x normal) and selling with a 4% stop-loss, an 8% trailing stop, or after 20 days, earns a better risk-adjusted return than SPY after costs.
spec.rationale: Cutting losses quickly while letting winners run should make average wins larger than average losses even with a low win rate. Counter-evidence on this exact data: last week's biggest gainers tended to UNDERPERFORM over the following week and month (5-day return raw IC about -0.016 at 5 days and -0.026 at 21 days). Tight stops on volatile stocks are also often hit by ordinary noise. Tested once, honestly, as the user's idea.
spec.prior_evidence: 5-day winners underperformed afterwards in this universe (raw IC about -0.016 at 5 days, -0.026 at 21 days).

rule.execution: buy at next open; hard stop intraday (gap exits at open); trailing stop and time exit at close

spec.decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 12 months against SPY. If any gate fails: close H5; do not try other gain thresholds, stop distances or holding periods on this data.

spec.hypothesis: The H5 breakout entry becomes profitable after costs when its stops are sized to each stock's volatility (a multiple of the 14-day ATR, chosen by walk-forward from a small grid) and each position is sized so a stopped-out trade loses about 1% of the account.
spec.rationale: H5's flat 4% stop was hit by ordinary noise in over half its trades. Volatility-scaled stops and risk-based sizing are standard practice. Expectation stated in advance: H5's entry showed no edge and 5-day winners underperformed afterwards in this universe, so exits alone are unlikely to create one. This tests that honestly, once.

signal.description: same entry as H5; stop and trailing distance in ATR multiples

spec.prior_evidence: H5 (same entry, fixed 4% stop) failed: profit factor 1.01. 5-day winners underperformed afterwards here.

rule.execution: buy at next open; ATR from the signal day; hard stop intraday (gap exits at open); trailing and time exits at close

calibration.selection: each year: highest Sharpe over all earlier years, averaged with grid neighbours (favours plateaus); ties go to the middle setting

validation.universe: S&P 400 mid-caps never in the S&P 500 (current members)

spec.decision_rule: If every walk-forward gate passes: validate ONCE on mid-caps; if that passes, freeze the chosen setting and forward-test 12 months against SPY. Any failure closes H6: no other grids, entries or selection rules on this data.
